notes: Stand-ins for Amazon Macie managed data identifiers. Macie publishes each identifier's keywords and some of its rules, not its implementation, so each entry is our approximation, with a fidelity tier.
keyword_mode: required = a keyword must be in the column name or near the occurrence in the cell; absent = reported only when no keyword is there; none = keywords are not considered.
keywords_from names an entry in keyword_lists. distance is how many characters between a keyword and the occurrence still count as near.
severity uses Macie's published severity table for the identifier's type: occurrences:LEVEL pairs.

notes: Macie: a 13-19 digit sequence that passes the Luhn check and uses a standard card number prefix for American Express, Dankort, Diners Club, Discover, Electron, JCB, Mastercard, UnionPay or Visa. Macie does not publish its prefix table; this one is ours.

Ours, not Macie's: groups separated by spaces or hyphens are also accepted (4-4-4-4, 4-4-4-4-3, Amex 4-6-5, Diners 4-6-4), with one separator throughout (David, 2026-11-01). Macie's docs only say digit sequence.

Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER. The format is ours, from the Social Security Administration's rules: AAA-GG-SSSS, no area 000, 666 or 900-999, no group 00, no serial 0000. Hyphens, spaces (one separator throughout) or none.
exclusions are ours: numbers widely published as examples, which SSA voided or never issued.
Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_NATIONAL_PROVIDER_IDENTIFIER. The format is ours, from CMS: 10 digits starting with 1 or 2, check digit by Luhn over 80840 followed by the first nine digits.
Macie: IBANs of up to 34 alphanumeric characters complying with ISO 13616, with no spaces, or with space or hyphen separators, validated by the Modulus 97 scheme. Keyword not required.
The parameter is the ISO 3166 country code, e.g. iban:GB. lengths are each country's IBAN length from the SWIFT IBAN registry (ours: Macie does not publish them).
Ours: separators only in the printed layout of groups of four, one separator throughout; letters in either case.
Macie publishes only the keywords for CANADA_SOCIAL_INSURANCE_NUMBER. The format is ours, from the Government of Canada: 9 digits, Luhn, printed 3-3-3; never starting with 0 or 8.
exclusions are ours: the number used as the example in Government of Canada publications.
Macie publishes only the keywords for UK_NHS_NUMBER. The format is ours, from NHS England: 10 digits, mod 11 check digit, printed 3-3-4.
Macie: a 17-character sequence that adheres to ISO 3779 and 3780, designed for worldwide use. Keyword required.

Ours: the VIN alphabet (no I, O or Q), a model-year character in position 10 (not U, Z or 0), letters and digits mixed. The North American check digit is not required: VINs from elsewhere don't have one. Fidelity B for that reason.

Macie publishes only the keywords for BRAZIL_CPF_NUMBER. The format is ours, from Receita Federal: 11 digits, ###.###.###-## or contiguous, two mod 11 check digits. One digit repeated (e.g. 111.111.111-11) passes the check but is never issued.

Macie publishes only the keywords for BRAZIL_CNPJ_NUMBER. The format is ours, from Receita Federal: 14 digits, ##.###.###/####-## or contiguous, two mod 11 check digits. One digit repeated is never issued.
Numeric CNPJs only. Alphanumeric CNPJs, issued from July 2026, are not detected yet.
Macie: CHILE_RUT_NUMBER detects RUN and RUT numbers and never reports numbers whose digits are all zeroes, e.g. 00000000-K.
The format is ours, from Chile's Servicio de Registro Civil: a 7 or 8 digit body, optional thousands dots, an optional hyphen, and a check character 0-9 or K by mod 11.
Macie: 16-digit SUBE card numbers that begin with 6061 and pass Luhn, with spaces, hyphens or no separator.

Macie's FRANCE_, GERMANY_, ITALY_, SPAIN_ and UK_BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER detect IBANs, which need no keyword, and the country's BBANs (ISO 13616), which need one. The UK one also detects domestic sort code and account numbers.
iban_lengths must match the iban detector's lengths; a test checks it.

BBAN shapes and layouts are ours, from the SWIFT IBAN registry and national practice. Checks: France's RIB key and Spain's two check digits. Italy's CIN letter is not checked: its rule is not confirmed from an authoritative source, and a wrong rule would miss real accounts. Germany and the UK have no generic BBAN check (account checks are bank-specific).

Macie publishes the keywords for SPAIN_DNI_NUMBER, and that 99999999, 99.999.999 and all zeroes are never reported. It also says it may report an Argentina DNI as a Spain DNI, or the other way around.

The format is ours, from Spain's Ministerio del Interior: 8 digits, optionally dotted, and a control letter (mod 23), optionally after a hyphen or space. We require the letter, so an Argentina DNI (digits only) is not reported; Macie's exclusions suggest it may accept digits alone. Fidelity B until the fidelity scan.
Macie publishes only the keywords for SPAIN_NIE_NUMBER: Spain's taxpayer list, shared with NIF and CIF.

The format is ours, from Spain's Ministerio del Interior: X, Y or Z, 7 digits and a control letter, the DNI's mod 23 with X, Y and Z as 0, 1 and 2. A hyphen or space may follow the first letter and precede the last. All zeroes are never reported, as Macie says of several taxpayer numbers.
Macie publishes only the keywords for INDIA_AADHAAR_NUMBER. The format is ours, from UIDAI: 12 digits, the last a Verhoeff check digit, never starting with 0 or 1, printed 4-4-4.
Macie publishes only the keywords for FRANCE_NATIONAL_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER (INSEE codes).

The format is ours, from INSEE: 15 characters, the department 2 digits or 2A or 2B, and a key of 97 minus the first 13 mod 97, with 2A and 2B as 19 and 18. Contiguous, 1-2-2-2-3-3-2 with spaces or dots, or with only the key apart. No rule on the sex digit or the month: a rule we cannot confirm would miss real numbers.
FRANCE_HEALTH_INSURANCE_NUMBER uses this detector too: the health insurance number is the NIR, with health keywords (carte vitale).
Macie publishes only the keywords for MEXICO_CURP_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from RENAPO: 4 letters, a real YYMMDD birth date, sex, a state code (or NE), 3 letters, a century character and a check digit over RENAPO's alphabet, which has Ñ after N. Ours: sex X is accepted as well as H and M, and RENAPO's list of 4 letter words never issued is not applied.
Macie lists ITALY_NATIONAL_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER as both a national identification and a taxpayer number, with one keyword list. It says Codice Fiscale.

The formats are ours, from the Agenzia delle Entrate: the 16 character code of a person, with omocodia letters for digits, a real birth day and month, and a check letter; and the 11 digit code of an organization (its partita IVA): 7 digits not all zero, an office code 001-100, 120, 121, 888 or 999, and a Luhn check digit, optionally after IT. The 11 digit codes go beyond what Macie documents: Macie says Codice Fiscale and its keywords include p. iva and partita i.v.a. (David, 2026-11-03: go beyond Macie at the margin when the check is clearly described).
Macie publishes only the keywords for GERMANY_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER, and says it detects Steueridentifikationsnummer numbers.

The format is ours, from the Bundeszentralamt fuer Steuern: 11 digits, no leading 0, in the first ten exactly one digit two or three times and the others once, and an ISO 7064 MOD 11,10 check digit. Printed 2-3-3-3.
Macie publishes only the keywords for ARGENTINA_INDIVIDUAL_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER (CUIL and CUIT), shared with the organization identifier.
The format is ours, from AFIP: 11 digits, printed 2-8-1 with hyphens or spaces, a 2 digit type, and a mod 11 check digit weighted 5 4 3 2 7 6 5 4 3 2.
Individuals' types are 20, 23, 24 and 27.
Macie publishes only the keywords for ARGENTINA_ORGANIZATION_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER, shared with the individual identifier, and scores it MEDIUM for 1-99 occurrences, HIGH from 100.
The format is ours, from AFIP: 11 digits, printed 2-8-1 with hyphens or spaces, a 2 digit type, and a mod 11 check digit weighted 5 4 3 2 7 6 5 4 3 2.
Organizations' types are 30, 33 and 34; the international types 50, 51 and 55 are put here too (ours).
Macie publishes only the keywords for AUSTRALIA_TAX_FILE_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from the ATO: 9 digits, printed 3-3-3, weighted 1 4 3 7 5 8 6 9 10 and divisible by 11. Older 8 digit TFNs are not detected: the published weights for them disagree, so the entry is partial.
Macie says UK_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER detects TRN and UTR numbers, and publishes only the keywords.

The format is ours, from HMRC: a UTR is 10 digits, printed 5-5, the first digit a check over the other nine, weighted 6 7 8 9 10 5 4 3 2. TRNs are not detected: their format could not be confirmed, so the entry is partial.

Macie says it detects CIF, NIE and NIF numbers for Spain, with SPAIN_NIE_NUMBER, SPAIN_NIF_NUMBER and SPAIN_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER sharing Spain's taxpayer keywords. Ours (David, 2026-11-03): NIF is a person's NIF, the DNI form or K, L or M; CIF is SPAIN_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER; NIEs stay with SPAIN_NIE_NUMBER, so nothing is counted twice. Fidelity B.
The format is ours, from the Agencia Tributaria: the DNI form (8 digits and the mod 23 letter, with Macie's DNI exclusions), or K, L or M, 7 digits and the DNI's letter over the 7 digits.

Macie says it detects CIF, NIE and NIF numbers for Spain, with SPAIN_NIE_NUMBER, SPAIN_NIF_NUMBER and SPAIN_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER sharing Spain's taxpayer keywords. Ours (David, 2026-11-03): NIF is a person's NIF, the DNI form or K, L or M; CIF is SPAIN_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER; NIEs stay with SPAIN_NIE_NUMBER, so nothing is counted twice. Fidelity B.

The format is ours, from the Agencia Tributaria: a type letter (A B C D E F G H J N P Q R S U V W), 7 digits, and a control digit or letter from the Luhn digit of the 7; either form is accepted, as sources disagree on which types use which.

Macie publishes the keywords, shared by the individual and organization identifiers, and that XAXX010101000 and XEXX010101000 are never reported; organizations are MEDIUM for 1-99, HIGH from 100. The format is ours, from the SAT: individuals 4 letters, organizations 3, then a real YYMMDD date and 3 characters. The final check digit is not checked: about 1.5% of RFCs in use have a wrong one (David, 2026-11-03). Fidelity B.

Macie publishes the keywords, shared by the individual and organization identifiers, and that XAXX010101000 and XEXX010101000 are never reported; organizations are MEDIUM for 1-99, HIGH from 100. The final check digit is not checked: about 1.5% of RFCs in use have a wrong one (David, 2026-11-03). Fidelity B.

Macie publishes only the keywords, shared by the individual and organization identifiers; organizations are MEDIUM for 1-99, HIGH from 100. The format is ours, from the DIAN: a body and a mod 11 check digit over prime weights, dotted, hyphenated or contiguous. Nothing in a NIT says person or organization; ours (David, 2026-11-03): a 9 digit body starting 8 or 9 is an organization's, any other 6 to 10 digit body a person's. Fidelity B.

Macie publishes only the keywords, shared by the individual and organization identifiers; organizations are MEDIUM for 1-99, HIGH from 100. The format is ours, from the DIAN: a body and a mod 11 check digit over prime weights, dotted, hyphenated or contiguous. Nothing in a NIT says person or organization; ours (David, 2026-11-03): a 9 digit body starting 8 or 9 is an organization's, any other 6 to 10 digit body a person's. Fidelity B.
Macie publishes only the keywords for FRANCE_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER (TINs).
The format is ours, from the DGFiP: the SPI number, 13 digits, printed 2-2-3-3-3, the first digit 0 to 3, the last three the first ten mod 511.
Macie: AWS_CREDENTIALS needs a keyword, and its two fictitious examples are never reported.
The format is ours: 40 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 / +. One that is all lower case hex (e.g. a SHA-1 hash) is not reported.
The examples are kept as SHA-256 hashes (exclusions_sha256): GitHub push protection rejects a repo holding even a published example key.
Macie: GCP_API_KEY needs a keyword and detects only the key string (keyString).
The format is ours: AIza and 35 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.

Macie: HTTP_BASIC_AUTH_HEADER needs no keyword, and needs a complete header, the field name and the scheme, per RFC 7617, e.g. Authorization: Basic QWxhZGRpbjpvcGVuIHNlc2FtZQ== and Proxy-Authorization: Basic dGVzdDoxMjPCow==.
Ours: the field and scheme in any case, as HTTP allows; the base64 token is not decoded.
Macie: JSON_WEB_TOKEN needs no keyword, and detects RFC 7519 JWS tokens, signed or unsigned.
Ours: three base64url parts; the header decodes to a JSON object with alg, the payload to a JSON object; the signature may be empty.
Macie: OPENSSH_PRIVATE_KEY needs no keyword; no other comments.
Ours: a whole BEGIN/END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY block in one cell.
Macie: PGP_PRIVATE_KEY needs no keyword; no other comments.
Ours: a whole BEGIN/END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK block in one cell, armor headers included.
Macie: PKCS (private keys) needs no keyword; no other comments.
Ours: a whole PRIVATE KEY (PKCS #8), ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY or RSA PRIVATE KEY (PKCS #1) block in one cell, and also EC and DSA PRIVATE KEY blocks, the same exposure though not PKCS.

Macie: PUTTY_PRIVATE_KEY needs no keyword, and detects keys with the standard headers in order: PuTTY-User-Key-File, Encryption, Comment, Public-Lines, Private-Lines, Private-MAC; values of letters, digits, hyphens and newlines, with / + = in the key lines and + in Private-MAC; no spaces, underscores or custom headers.
Ours: exactly that.
Macie: STRIPE_CREDENTIALS needs no keyword, and never reports its two code examples, a secret and a publishable test key, so test and publishable keys are reported.
The format is ours: sk_, pk_ or rk_, live_ or test_, and at least 24 letters and digits.
The examples are kept as SHA-256 hashes (exclusions_sha256): GitHub push protection rejects a repo holding even a published example key.
Macie publishes only the keywords for US_DRUG_ENFORCEMENT_AGENCY_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from the DEA: a registrant type letter, the registrant's initial (or 9), 7 digits, the last a check digit: the 1st, 3rd and 5th digits plus twice the 2nd, 4th and 6th, last digit. Ours: any type letter, so new registrant types are not missed.
Macie lists USA_MEDICARE_BENEFICIARY_IDENTIFIER with health insurance numbers and publishes only its keywords.

The format is ours, from CMS: 11 characters by position (1-9, letter, letter or digit, digit, letter, letter or digit, digit, letter, letter, digit, digit), letters never S L O I B Z, optional dashes after the 4th and 7th. CMS's published example 1EG4-TE5-MK73 is excluded (ours).
Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_INDIVIDUAL_TAX_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from the IRS: 9, two digits, middle digits 50-65, 70-88, 90-92 or 94-99 (the ranges since 2011; python-stdnum still has only 70-99), four digits; hyphens or spaces, one separator, or none.
Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_HEALTH_INSURANCE_CLAIM_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from CMS: an SSN, by the SSA rules, and a beneficiary identification code of a letter and an optional letter or digit. Railroad Retirement Board numbers are not detected, so the entry is partial. Fidelity B.
Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_NATIONAL_DRUG_CODE.
The format is ours, from the FDA: 10 digits as 4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1, the 11 digit 5-4-2 billing form, or 10 or 11 digits contiguous. There is no check digit. Fidelity B.
Macie publishes only the keywords for USA_HEALTHCARE_PROCEDURE_CODE, which include current procedural terminology.
The format is ours, from CMS and the AMA: HCPCS Level II, a letter A-V and 4 digits; and CPT, 5 digits, or 4 digits and F, T or U. There is no check digit. Fidelity B.
Macie publishes only the keywords for GERMANY_NATIONAL_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER (German National Identity Card numbers).

The format is ours, from the BMI: 9 characters of 0-9 and C F G H J K L M N P R T V W X Y Z, then an ICAO 9303 check digit (7 3 1). The official specimen is T220001293. Some of Macie's keywords are broad (id number, insurance number), and an all digit number passes the check one time in ten, so this can over-report. Fidelity B.
Macie: CREDIT_CARD_MAGNETIC_STRIPE needs a keyword and supports tracks 1 and 2.

The format is ours, from ISO/IEC 7813: track 1 %B, card number, ^, name, ^, YYMM, service code, discretionary data, ?; track 2 ;, card number, =, YYMM, service code, discretionary digits, ?. Sentinels may be missing. The card number must pass Luhn and the month must be 01-12.
Macie publishes only the keywords for UK_NATIONAL_INSURANCE_NUMBER.

The format is ours, from HMRC (NIM39110): two prefix letters, 6 digits, a suffix A to D, contiguous or spaced as AB 12 34 56 C. D F I Q U V are never a prefix letter, O is never the second, and the prefixes BG GB KN NK NT TN ZZ are not used.
Macie: BANK_ACCOUNT_NUMBER detects Canadian and US bank account numbers that are 9-17 digit sequences without spaces, with a keyword. That is the whole format.
Macie publishes only the keywords for CREDIT_CARD_SECURITY_CODE, and scores it MEDIUM for one occurrence, HIGH from two.
The format is ours: the 3 digit CVV/CVC or the 4 digit American Express CID. The keyword does nearly all the work; fidelity B.
Macie publishes only the keywords for CANADA_PASSPORT_NUMBER, and scores passport numbers MEDIUM for one occurrence, HIGH from two.
The format is ours: IRCC: a Canadian passport number has 8 characters, 2 letters then 6 digits (https://www.ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=1446).
Macie publishes only the keywords for FRANCE_PASSPORT_NUMBER, and scores passport numbers MEDIUM for one occurrence, HIGH from two.

The format is ours: 2 digits, 2 letters, 5 digits (European Commission, OCS analysis, document number formats: https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/2012-12/OCS%20Analysis%20-%20Document%20ID%20V1%203%202.pdf).
Macie publishes only the keywords for GERMANY_PASSPORT_NUMBER, and scores passport numbers MEDIUM for one occurrence, HIGH from two.

The format is ours: 9 characters of digits and C F G H J K L M N P R T V W X Y Z; the Auswaertiges Amt leaves out vowels and B D Q S. Ours: the first is C F G H J or K, as detection rules for German passports have it. The MRZ check digit is not part of the printed number.
Macie publishes only the keywords for ITALY_PASSPORT_NUMBER, and scores passport numbers MEDIUM for one occurrence, HIGH from two.

Macie publishes only the keywords for INDIA_DRIVERS_LICENSE, and scores driver's license numbers LOW for one occurrence, MEDIUM from 2, HIGH from 100.

The format is ours: Microsoft Purview sensitive information type definitions (learn.microsoft.com/purview/sit-defn-<country>-drivers-license-number), a vendor's detection patterns, not the issuer's: the DNI (8 digits and a letter or digit) or the NIE of a foreigner. Microsoft checks the control letter; ours: the shape only, as the DNI and NIE identifiers already check the letter.
Macie publishes only the keywords for UK_DRIVERS_LICENSE, and scores driver's license numbers LOW for one occurrence, MEDIUM from 2, HIGH from 100.

The format is ours: The DVLA's structure: 5 characters of the surname (9 for padding), a decade digit, the month (plus 50 for women, so its first digit is 0 1 5 or 6), the day, the year digit, 2 initials (9 for padding), a digit, 2 check letters, and an optional 2 digit issue number. Microsoft's 18 character description does not match the DVLA layout, so it is not used (ours).
Macie publishes only the keywords for DRIVERS_LICENSE, and scores driver's license numbers LOW for one occurrence, MEDIUM from 2, HIGH from 100.

The format is ours: The union of the states' formats (David, 2026-11-05: one identifier, as Macie has), each tagged with its states; from Skyhigh Security's DLP reference (success.skyhighsecurity.com, U.S. Driver's License Numbers), a vendor's table, not the DMVs'. Washington is the DOL's WDL format since 2018; older Washington numbers are not detected (ours).
Macie publishes the keywords for ARGENTINA_DNI_NUMBER, and that it does not report 99999999, 99.999.999 or numbers of only zeroes.
The format is ours (RENAPER): 7 or 8 digits, contiguous or with dots as 12.345.678.
Macie says it might report an Argentine DNI as a Spanish one, or the other way around. Ours: a Spanish DNI needs its check letter, so 8 digits alone are only Argentina's.
Macie publishes only the keywords for BRAZIL_RG_NUMBER.

The format is ours: RG numbers are issued by each state. We take the common Sao Paulo shape, 8 digits and a check character (a digit or X), as 12.345.678-9, 12345678-9 or 123456789. The check character is not verified: it is not computed the same way in every state.
Macie publishes only the keywords for COLOMBIA_CITIZENSHIP_CARD_NUMBER.
The format is ours (Registraduria Nacional): 6 to 10 digits, contiguous or with dots between thousands as 1.234.567.890. The number has no check digit.
Macie publishes only the keywords for CANADA_NATIONAL_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER, its permanent residence number.
The format is ours: the IRCC client identifier (UCI) printed on the permanent resident card, 8 or 10 digits, as 1234-5678 or 12-3456-7890. The card's own document number is not included.
Macie publishes only the keywords for INDIA_PERMANENT_ACCOUNT_NUMBER.

The format is ours (Income Tax Department): 5 letters, 4 digits and a letter, as ABCPE1234F. The fourth letter is the holder type: A B C F G H J L P or T. The last letter is a check character whose rule is not published, so it is not verified.
Macie publishes only the keywords for UK_ELECTORAL_ROLL_NUMBER.
The format is ours, as Microsoft Purview describes it: a polling district's two letters and an elector number of 1 to 4 digits, as AB123.
Macie publishes the keywords for BRAZIL_CEP_CODE, that it finds only the CEP part of an address, and scores mailing addresses LOW for one occurrence, MEDIUM from 2, HIGH from 100.
The format is ours (Correios): 8 digits, as 01310-100, 01310100 or 01.310-100.
